external_check_reason: on the candidate lists themselves (sources no rule selects and no list contains), the 34-feature model's equal-burden tier carries more low-redshift objects by every available measure: catalog photo-z < 3 for 34.9% of the tier against 21.5% (known LRDs: 15 of 147 = 10.2%; the rules' own novel picks: 40.8%), and a secure archival z <= 3 within 0.5 arcsec for 21 against 8 sources (secure z > 3: 15 against 17). The extra picks with archival low-z redshifts have larger half-light radii and higher concentration indices than the untested picks, consistent with the aperture-concentration features admitting compact low-z galaxies that the z > 3 negatives never penalise.

rule_outcome: no challenger met the pre-stated rule: the 34-feature trees gain one positive and no rule-missed and win 3 of 5 regions; the MLP wins 2 of 5; the blend wins 3 of 5. The 30-feature incumbent of the plan of record therefore stays deployed by the rule itself, not by a tie-break.
exploratory_comparisons: two comparisons made after the rule, both exploratory and not part of it: (1) the 34-feature set's lower targeted-negative selection rate (48 vs 70), which counts only z > 3 targets; (2) the photo-z and archival-redshift make-up of the two candidate lists. During the build the 34-feature model was briefly chosen on (1) and reverted on (2); the sequence is in decision_sequence. Because (2) was consulted, the archive comparison of the deployed candidates is post hoc and selection-influenced, not an independent test.
